'''Teresa Mary Anderson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|MBE}} (born 1962) is a British physicist and the director of the [[University of Manchester]]'s Discovery Centre at [[Jodrell Bank Observatory]]. She is a professor at the [[University of Manchester]] and the curator of science at the Bluedot Festival.

== Education ==
Anderson completed an undergraduate degree in the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Manchester|School of Physics]] at the [[University of Manchester]] in 1986.{{citation needed|date=April 2018}} She earned a Masters in Instrumentation and Analytical Science.{{when|date=April 2018}} She received a [[PhD]] in Electrical Engineering from the [[University of Edinburgh]]<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|first=Teresa Mary|last=Anderson|title=MICADO : a system of decision support software for micro hydro power in Nepal |hdl=1842/13407 |id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.640491 }}|degree=PhD|year=1992}} {{free access}}</ref>
<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/people/library-cultural-institutions-profiles/|title=Library and visitor attractions profiles {{!}} The University of Manchester|work=The University of Manchester|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dev.ed.ac.uk/gradassoc/documents/journals/Volume_46/UofE%20Journal%20Vol%2046,%20No%202%20-%202013.pdf|title=University of Edinburgh Journal|date=2013|website=Edinburgh University|access-date=2018-04-02}}</ref> where her thesis was on developing [[renewable energy]] systems in [[Nepal]].<ref name=phd/> She also holds a Master's degree in Fine Art from the [[Birmingham Institute of Art and Design]].{{citation needed|date=April 2018}}

== Career ==
After graduating she went on to work for [[Practical Action]], a charity which uses technology to challenge poverty in developing countries.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.womanthology.co.uk/intergalactic-festival-music-science-arts-culture-exploration-space-meet-professor-teresa-anderson-science-culture-director-bluedot/|title=The intergalactic festival where music, science, arts, culture and the exploration of space meet - Professor Teresa Anderson MBE, Science-Culture Director of Bluedot - Womanthology|date=2017-04-19|work=Womanthology|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en-US}}</ref> Anderson worked in the [[Himalayas]], [[Sri Lanka]] and the [[South America]]n rainforest.<ref name=":0" />  She returned to the UK to work with the [[Science Policy Research Unit]] and the [[University of Warwick]] on Renewable Energy and Climate Change Policy.<ref name=":2" /> Anderson spent three years creating the UK [[Café Scientifique]] network with Duncan Dallas and Tom Shakespeare, which has now established a significant national and international reputation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2003/may/22/research.science1|title=And now for the scientifique bit|last=Moss|first=Stephen|date=2003-05-22|website=The Guardian|language=en|access-date=2018-04-04}}</ref> She then joined [[Nesta (charity)|NESTA]] to work on Science-Culture-Arts policy.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencecentres.org.uk/about/past-trustees/dr-teresa-anderson/|title=Dr Teresa Anderson|website=The Association for Science and Discovery Centres|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref>

===Jodrell Bank===
In 2006, Anderson joined [[Jodrell Bank Observatory]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://blue-stocking.org.uk/2017/04/17/an-interview-with-professor-teresa-anderson-mbe/|title=An Interview with Professor Teresa Anderson MBE|date=2017-04-17|work=blue-stocking|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2010 she began to set up the Discovery Centre, which opened in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jb.man.ac.uk/news/2010/discovery/|title=Jodrell Bank plans new 'live science' visitor centre {{!}} Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics|last=O'Brien|first=Tim|website=www.jb.man.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fcbstudios.com/index.php?p=work/view/jodrell-bank|title=Jodrell Bank {{!}} Work {{!}} FCBStudios|website=fcbstudios.com|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=http://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/jodrell-bank-duo-honoured-for-innovative-science-communication/|title=Jodrell Bank duo honoured for innovative science communication|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en}}</ref> Today Anderson is Director of the Discovery Centre at [[Jodrell Bank Observatory]] which welcomes over 185,000 visitors per year.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.discoverthebluedot.com/profile/teresa-anderson|title=Teresa Anderson – Bluedot Festival|website=Bluedot Festival|language=en|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref> The Jodrell Bank schools programme started in 2012 and sees 26,000 school children visit per year.<ref name=":4" /> The Centre is run as a [[Social enterprise]] and receives very little funding.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=ST%2FP001564%2F1|title=Real Science Pulsar Workshop at Jodrell Bank Discovery Centre|website=UKRI Gateway|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref>

The centre run ''Live from Jodrell Bank'' science-music events, including bands such as [[The Flaming Lips]], [[New Order (band)|New Order]] and [[Elbow (band)|Elbow]] alongside scientific research such as [[graphene]] and the [[Large Hadron Collider]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cheshire-live.co.uk/news/chester-cheshire-news/amazed-science-jodrell-bank-brings-6809326|title=Science festival aims to amaze youngsters|last=Smith|first=Stephen|date=2014-03-13|work=chesterchronicle|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref> The Centre has won many awards, including ''Marketing Cheshire''<nowiki/>'s Team of the Year and the ''[[UK Festival Awards]]'' Extreme Creativity award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jodrellbank.manchester.ac.uk/outreach/jodrell-bank-discovery-centre/|title=Jodrell Bank Discovery Centre ===Awards and honours===
Anderson was recognised for her services to Astrophysics in 2013, when the Queen awarded her an MBE.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.labmate-online.com/news/news-and-views/5/cern/cern-director-receives-queenrsquos-honours/25744|title=CERN Director Receives Queen's Honours Labmate Online|website=www.labmate-online.com|language=en|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/alumni/services/news/news-archive/2013-news/birthdayhonours|title=Birthday Honours 2013|work=The University of Edinburgh|access-date=2018-04-03|language=en}}</ref> She won the 2014 [[Institute of Physics]] [[Kelvin Prize]] for Public Engagement with physics, alongside [[Tim O'Brien (astronomer)|Tim O'Brien]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/kelvin/medallists/page_63435.html|title=2014 Kelvin medal and prize|last=Physics|first=Institute of|website=www.iop.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-04-03|archive-date=4 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180404073046/http://www.iop.org/about/awards/gold/kelvin/medallists/page_63435.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Anderson was Chair of the Association of Science and Discovery Centres in 2010, a role she held until 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/company/06798106/officers|title=THE ASSOCIATION FOR SCIENCE AND DISCOVERY CENTRES - Officers (free information from Companies House)|website=beta.companieshouse.gov.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> Anderson is on the Advisory Panel for the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]] Public Engagement strategy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://stfc.ukri.org/about-us/how-we-are-governed/advisory-boards-panels-committees/advisory-panel-for-public-engagement/|title=Advisory Panel for Public Engagement - Science and Technology Facilities Council|website=stfc.ukri.org|language=en|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref> She is a Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ras.org.uk/publications/224-news-2013/2292-ras-congratulates-honoured-fellows|title=RAS congratulates honoured Fellows|last=Smith|first=Keith|website=www.ras.org.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref>

In 2015 Anderson became Chair of the [[Daphne Jackson Trust]], a charity which supports scientists in their return-to-work following career breaks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.daphnejackson.org/news/stories/2015/teresa_anderson_mbe_to_chair_daphne_jackson_trusts_board_of_trustees.htm|title=Teresa Anderson MBE, to chair Daphne Jackson Trust's Board of Trustees|last=caroline.cross@surrey.ac.uk|first=Caroline Cross|website=www.daphnejackson.org|language=EN|access-date=2018-04-03|archive-date=3 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403234935/http://www.daphnejackson.org/news/stories/2015/teresa_anderson_mbe_to_chair_daphne_jackson_trusts_board_of_trustees.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.daphnejackson.org/about/trustees/|title=Trustees|last=caroline.cross@surrey.ac.uk|first=Caroline Cross|website=www.daphnejackson.org|language=EN|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.staffnet.manchester.ac.uk/news/display/?id=14177|title=Teresa Anderson MBE to chair Daphne Jackson Trust's Board of Trustees {{!}} StaffNet {{!}} The University of Manchester|website=www.staffnet.manchester.ac.uk|access-date=2018-04-03}}</ref>
